assessment.summary: User selected the complete safe-diagnostics, historical-retrieval and recipient-bound egress design. Documentation only; runtime implementation and measured limits remain pending.

decision.scope: Design documents and implementation handoff; no runtime implementation, commit or push in this task.

nonNegotiables: Sensitive logs must not enter model services, including through first returns, replay, summarization and retrieval.
Old results expose only contract-approved metadata.
New retrieval reads the exact published first-return safe projection, not additional raw body.
MCP source allowlisting does not imply content safety or outbound permission.
Historical tests do not automatically satisfy current delivery gates.
Outbound data uses trusted fixed artifacts and recipient-specific authorization; generic free text is closed by default.
JSON only; authoritative state changes require typed events and exact expected versions.
Page size, cumulative limits, context target and retention are measurement decisions.
assumptions: No new performance or real-model experiments ran in this documentation task.
Whole-repository Docker mounts do not attest to safe diagnostic inputs.
F20/F21 fixes and later source drift must be independently rechecked.

opportunities.title: Safe diagnostics, historical retrieval and content egress
opportunities.summary: Unify first-return/replay visibility, scoped historical access and recipient-bound dispatch without elevating retrieved text into authority.
opportunities.diagnosis: Result persistence, context projection and action authorization do not by themselves prove content is allowed for each recipient.

evidence.claim: Historical follow-up memory gaps record incomplete request accounting; individual status must be checked against current source.
The recorded capacity gap covers instruction/tool-definition accounting and an independent final gate.
Tool results enter context; compaction precedes final tool snapshot and ModelRequest construction. Related ledger/redaction/recovery sources are hashed in the evidence inventory.
Test return serialization includes stdout/stderr; MCP envelope/redaction and finalization evidence are distinct paths.
Docker disables network but mounts the whole repository read-only; this does not prove secret-free input.
Action documents bind canonical arguments, target and MCP identities; the inspected fields do not provide a general data-release contract.
The latest report records zero seed items against 19 loop items and an earlier committed compaction. The exact construction-path defect remains to be verified.
Historical F21 report describes CheckpointError escaping terminalization; c9dfb5e claims a fix, not revalidated in this documentation task.
Session projections populate future context, so restoration and summarization require the same model-ingress boundary.

desiredInvariants: Every model-visible item has trusted provenance and current audience authorization.
Unknown bodies yield only explicitly releasable metadata.
Result identity and current applicability remain distinct.
Immutable publication precedes visibility; indexes are rebuildable.
Final model requests account for all input and output reserve.
Egress binds actual payload, recipient, artifact version, policy and tool identity.
